$schema: Instance config for a loopd control panel. Customize, then commit. TRACKED, so every value here is a statement both clones of a shared bundle read; the per-machine half lives beside it in the gitignored instance.config.local.json, whose overridable set is listed in ONE place -- SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'. `models` and `roleTiers` below are SEEDED into that local file by /loopd:init and are kept here as the FALLBACK: with neither layer, scripts/resolve-model.sh resolves to nothing and every agent inherits the session model.
$group: OPTIONAL short name for this bundle -- the label the board, print-board.sh and the seeded <group>.code-workspace use. ABSENT (or null, as here) the group is the bundle DIRECTORY's name minus a bundle prefix (`_ai-bridge-` or `_loopd-`), which is the behaviour every bundle has today. Set it and the directory can be renamed freely without the board relabelling the bundle or the KB indexer losing track of it. TRACKED, never per-machine: a bundle has one name and both clones of a shared bundle must agree on it.
$people: EXAMPLE ONLY -- replace both entries below with your team's real GitHub login -> commit email pairs, HERE in this instance. The loopd template is public, so it ships placeholder logins VERIFIED UNCLAIMED on github.com (example-user-007/008 both 404) and addresses at example.com, which RFC 2606 reserves and which cannot receive mail. If you write a new example, verify the login is unclaimed the same way: a plausible name like alice or bob is a real account, and an example naming a stranger is an example someone copies. The address is PER-INSTANCE, not per-person: the same login belongs to a different address in each group's bundle, because the address says which entity the work belongs to -- so never derive it from the login, and never move it into instance.config.local.json (that file says which login this clone IS). Used by scripts/commit-as.sh so each clone authors commits as the human running it; see SCHEMA.md 'Per-machine config overrides'. (/loopd:init offers to collect these when it stamps a NEW bundle at a terminal; it never overwrites what is already here.)
$commitAttribution: Whether a role agent ends a TARGET-REPO commit with the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer. `claude` (the default, and what an absent key means) keeps it, because Claude did co-author the commit and the trailer is simply true; `none` is the opt-out for an organisation that requires one, and drops both the trailer and any session URL. PER-MACHINE OVERRIDABLE -- SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'. No agent ever reads this key: scripts/dispatch-brief.sh resolves it and the dispatch brief carries the answer, so one resolver answers for every role. It does NOT reach scripts/commit-as.sh, which authors THIS bundle's own commits as the role and adds no trailer at any setting.
$ticketPrefix: OPTIONAL Jira-shaped project key (e.g. "ABC") appended to every PR title a role agent opens. ABSENT (or null, as here) => NO TAG: the title is `<type>: <subject>` and nothing follows it. Set, titles end `[ABC-<n>]` with the id the task names, or `[ABC-0]` when it names none; agents never invent an id or guess a prefix. A value that is not uppercase letters, digits and underscores is read as absent. TRACKED, never per-machine: it names the organisation's ticket system. No agent reads this key: scripts/dispatch-brief.sh resolves it into the brief's `## PR title`, as it does commitAttribution.
$knowledge: OPTIONAL. Mount this bundle's knowledge/ from ANOTHER repository, so several bundles (and people on other harnesses) share one canonical KB. Three fields: `repo` ("org/name", cloned over the SAME TRANSPORT AND HOST as this bundle's own origin remote -- or a full URL, which is taken verbatim and is how you override that), `path` ("/" for the repo root, or "knowledge" for a top-level folder of that name inside a shared repo) and an optional `ref`, which must name a BRANCH -- a tag or a SHA checks out a detached HEAD the write path cannot push, and both are refused by name. ABSENT (or null, as here) NOTHING CHANGES: knowledge/ stays a plain folder of this bundle's own repo. Set, /loopd:init clones it into knowledge/ as a nested, gitignored clone -- a REAL directory, never a symlink and never a submodule -- one per bundle, never shared between two bundles on one machine. The clone is made and refreshed by plugin/scripts/kb-sync.sh, which is also the ONLY writer: role agents return Findings in their result and the tick commits them. SCHEMA.md, 'A mounted knowledge base'.
$knowledgeSources: OPTIONAL read-only mounts, same scheme as `knowledge` above and the same script: each entry is { repo, path?, ref? } and is cloned to knowledge-sources/<repo-name>/. Never written, never pushed, never index-regenerated -- a write attempted against one is refused by name. Use it for a generated or third-party corpus you read but never curate.
$maxPrLoc: The LINE COUNT past which a PR-opening role agent proposes a split. Absent => 500, which is the number every doc naming this key states, because those docs are read inside bundles whose config predates it -- this seed ships the key PRESENT at 2000, so a freshly stamped bundle uses 2000 and never the fallback. Raise it for fewer, larger PRs (and so fewer external-reviewer sessions); lower it for tighter review units. Never a gate and never a review criterion: the agent SAYS SO in the PR body and opens the PR anyway, because generated boilerplate, codemods and dense logic all move the real number.
$maxPrFiles: The FILE COUNT past which a PR-opening role agent proposes a split, and past which the project-manager proposes splitting a task before dispatch. Absent => 100. It sits beside maxPrLoc because the two count different things and the reviewer counts THIS one: CodeRabbit's free plan refuses a pull request over 100 files outright, before any quota question (measured 2026-09-05, ai-bridge#122 at 147 files), and a `git mv` sweep is 1 file per rename while barely moving the line count. Same status as maxPrLoc in every other respect: the agent SAYS SO and opens the PR anyway, never a gate and never a review criterion.
$maxStallRounds: How many CONSECUTIVE rounds a task may end on the SAME blocker before the PM stops re-dispatching it. Absent => 2, which is the number every doc naming this key states, because those docs are read inside bundles whose config predates it. At the cap the tick runs scripts/stall-counter.sh escalate: status becomes blocked, the blocker is recorded under # Notes, and ONE line goes to AWAITING.md, because the human is this loop's escalation path and a fresh agent at the same wall is not. It is NOT a timeout and not a slow-PR guard: PR activity (a new commit, a new review thread), a changed blocker and a human edit each reset the counter, so only genuine repetition ever reaches the cap. 1 escalates on the first repeat; raise it where an intermittent check is expected to clear itself.
$maxRepeatedToolCalls: How many times ONE dispatched agent may make the SAME tool call -- same tool name, same arguments -- in a row before plugin/hooks/agent-control.sh refuses it. Absent from BOTH config layers => OFF: nothing is hashed, counted or written, so a bundle that predates this key is unaffected and this seed ships it PRESENT at 3 so a freshly stamped bundle is guarded. It needs the control surface armed (scripts/control.sh arm), like every other verb that hook enforces. Below 2 reads as off -- 1 would refuse the first call of every kind. The breach is a `deny`, never a kill: the agent keeps its worktree and its index and reports, and the refusal lifts the moment it makes a DIFFERENT call. Read-only waits (`gh pr checks`, `gh run view|watch|list`, `gh pr view`, `sleep`) are a legitimate poll and are never counted, however often they repeat. PER-MACHINE OVERRIDABLE -- SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'.
$maxAgentMinutes: The WALL-CLOCK budget for ONE dispatched agent, in minutes, for every role `roleMinutes` does not name -- `roleMinutes: {"<role>": <n>}` sets one role's, merged per role like roleTiers, and the project-manager tick defaults to 180 because it walks the whole bundle. Absent from BOTH config layers => 45; 0 or anything that is not a positive integer reads as OFF. Past the budget, plugin/hooks/agent-control.sh refuses the agent's next tool call with a `deny` naming the elapsed time and the budget, and the refusal is a WRAP-UP instruction: commit and push what you have, open or update the PR, report. A read-only call is still allowed so that report can be accurate -- Read, Grep, Glob, and a Bash made only of `git add|commit|push`, `commit-as.sh`, `cd` and `gh pr create|edit|view|checks` (a quoted message may span lines and carry parentheses; no pipe, redirect or unquoted substitution) -- and Edit, Write and every other Bash are refused. It needs the control surface armed (scripts/control.sh arm), like every other verb that hook enforces. The clock starts at the SubagentStart record under .claude/control/agents.d/, falling back to the oldest timestamp the subagent transcript carries; SubagentStop drops it, so a resumed agent is given a fresh budget. It is a deny, never a kill: the agent keeps its worktree and its index. PER-MACHINE OVERRIDABLE -- SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'.
$account: OPTIONAL label naming which Claude account this bundle belongs to, e.g. "proceso". A LABEL, never a credential. Inert on its own: it does anything only while the loopd-accounts companion (from core's own marketplace) is installed, which ships the launcher that starts claude on that account and makes plugin/scripts/resolve-account.sh answer. With both, the welcome banner names the active account and WARNS in red when the session is on a different one and in yellow when it is on none, so a bundle can never quietly run on the other organisation's plan. The account's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR lives under $AI_BRIDGE_ACCOUNTS_HOME (default ~/.claude-accounts) and the launcher refuses one inside a bundle or any git work tree, so no credential can reach this repo.
$board: ON BY DEFAULT, and it is read at BOTH ends of the lifecycle. true (or absent) => /loopd:init creates SNAPSHOT.json when missing on any stamp, so this instance appears on the terminal board, AND each /loopd:dispatch tick re-renders the page to .loopd/.board-live/board.html (derived and gitignored, served by bundle-paths.sh) and reports that path. false => the snapshot is never created, the installer says so, and the tick renders nothing and says nothing. NOTHING IS COMMITTED AND NOTHING IS ACCOUNT-SCOPED: the page is derived, so no copy leaves this machine unless you publish one yourself. (The account-scoped publish path, and the config key that recorded its URL, were deleted: only the publishing account could ever update the page, and it vanished from under its own owner at the next login.) Question TEXT is never in the snapshot or the page file; only scripts/board-serve.sh's localhost response shows it. scripts/watch-board.sh renders the same file continuously if you want it live between ticks.
$roles: Agents the PM may dispatch as TASK ASSIGNEES. Not every configured agent belongs here — `plan-architect` is deliberately absent: `/plan` and the PM's approach critique dispatch it directly, and no task is ever assigned to it. See `$roleTiers` and SCHEMA.md 'type: Agent'.
$models: Which model alias each TIER costs. PER-MACHINE SPEND, and /loopd:init seeds this key into instance.config.local.json on any stamp that finds it missing there -- so on a stamped instance the LOCAL copy is the one in force and the session banner's FROM column reads `local`. This tracked copy stays as the fallback and as the seed source: removing it would let an unseeded instance resolve to nothing, and an agent that resolves to nothing inherits the session model with no error. Edit the LOCAL file to change what this machine pays; a partial local map overrides entry by entry, and the installer never tops it up. See SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'.
$roleTiers: PER-MACHINE SPEND, seeded and overridden exactly as `models` above (see `$models`). The model tier for ANY agent this instance dispatches, including ones no task is ever assigned to — broader than `roles`. `plan-architect: apex` here and nowhere in `roles` is the intentional case: `models.apex` today affects exactly that one agent, which appears in no `roles` list, so 'what does apex cost me?' is unanswerable from `roles` alone. `explorer: light` is the second: it prices the Explore subagent a role agent delegates a broad read to (CONVENTIONS.md), which is a harness subagent type and never a task assignee. Do not delete either row to make the two lists match; see SCHEMA.md 'type: Agent' and tests/roles-roletiers-asymmetry.test.sh.
